title: Economic growth
competency: Explain economic growth, calculate the growth rate and per capita income, and explain the limits of these measures and the HDI.

keywords.def: An increase in the capacity of an economy to produce goods and services.
The rate at which real GDP increases over a period: (real GDPₜ − real GDPₜ₋₁) ÷ real GDPₜ₋₁ × 100.
Total (real) GNP divided by total population: the average income per person.
HDI: the UNDP "quality of life index" that combines several development indicators into one number.

en.text: Economic growth is an increase in the capacity of an economy to produce goods and services; it is needed for higher incomes and living standards. The economic growth rate is the rate at which real GDP rises: (real GDPₜ − real GDPₜ₋₁) ÷ real GDPₜ₋₁ × 100. Growth comes from more labour, land and capital and higher productivity, supported by the rule of law and protection of property and contract rights.

am.text: ኢኮኖሚያዊ እድገት የማምረት አቅም መጨመር ነው። የእድገት መጠን የእውነተኛ ምርት ለውጥ ለቀድሞው ምርት ተካፍሎ በ100 ሲባዛ ነው።

screens.title: Economic growth
paras: Economic growth is an increase in the capacity to produce goods and services.
It is needed for high incomes and higher living standards.
Higher GDP per capita means better diet, health, life expectancy and education.
GDP expands or shrinks with the economic environment.
The economic growth rate is the rate at which real GDP rises over a period.

screens.title: Sources of growth
paras: More factors of production: labour, land, capital.
Higher productivity of those factors.
Institutions: rule of law, protection of property and contract rights.
These let markets work effectively and efficiently.

screens.title: Growth-rate formula
screens.text: The book gives no formula; this is the standard one.
steps: Growth rate = (real GDPₜ − real GDPₜ₋₁) ÷ real GDPₜ₋₁ × 100.

defs: An increase in the capacity of an economy to produce goods and services.
The rate at which real GDP increases over a period: (real GDPₜ − real GDPₜ₋₁) ÷ real GDPₜ₋₁ × 100.

ideas.name: Per capita income and the HDI

en.text: Real income is often understated in developing countries because of subsistence output, under-reporting, a non-monetary sector, price distortions and no deduction for pollution. Simple GDP growth also ignores price changes and population growth, so economists use real per capita income: GNP ÷ population. Because an average hides how income is shared and ignores health and education, the UNDP built the Human Development Index (HDI), a "quality of life index".

am.text: የነፍስ ወከፍ ገቢ = ጠቅላላ ብሔራዊ ምርት ÷ የሕዝብ ብዛት። ይህ አማካይ ስለሆነ ትምህርትና ጤናን አያሳይም፤ ስለዚህ የተባበሩት መንግሥታት የሰው ልማት መለኪያ (HDI) ተዘጋጀ።

screens.title: More output, more people
screens.ask: Move GDP growth and population growth. When does income per person rise? When does it fall?
screens.note: Roughly: growth per person ≈ GNP growth − population growth.

screens.title: Why income is understated in developing countries
paras: a) Most people are subsistence farmers; output for their own use is not correctly reported.
b) People under-report income for fear of tax; tax systems are weak.
c) No allowance is made for the non-monetary sector.
d) Prices are much more distorted.
e) Pollution costs are not deducted (Sweden and the Netherlands do deduct them).

screens.title: Two limits of the simple growth measure
paras: 1. National income is in value terms; it rises when prices rise, even if output is the same.
2. It ignores population growth, which can be faster than income growth.
Fix: measure growth as a rise in real per capita income.
Per capita income = total GNP ÷ total population.

screens.title: Beyond per capita income: the HDI
paras: Per capita income is an average: it "conceals more than it reveals".
It treats growth and development as the same thing.
Development also needs income distribution, education and health.
The UNDP Human Development Index (HDI) is called the "quality of life index".
It compresses several indicators into one composite index.
Today the HDI uses life expectancy, years of schooling and GNI per capita; it runs from 0 to 1.
screens.note: The last line corrects the book, which calls the HDI purely non-monetary.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Total (real) GNP divided by total population: the average income per person.
HDI: the UNDP "quality of life index" that combines several development indicators into one number.

screens.why: p.7: the ratio of total GNP to total population.

screens.ask: Real GNP = 360 bn Birr; population = 120 million. Per capita income = ___ Birr

screens.text: Real GNP grows 4 % while population grows 6 %. Real per capita income
screens.why: Growth per person ≈ 4 − 6 = −2 %. Population grew faster than income.

screens.text: Why is real income often understated in developing countries?
pool: People under-report income for fear of tax
The non-monetary sector is left out
a: People under-report income for fear of tax
The non-monetary sector is left out
screens.why: p.7 reasons a–c. The last two options are the opposite of the book.

screens.text: Per capita income shows how income is shared among people.
screens.why: It is an average; it says nothing about distribution. That is one of its limits.
screens.clue: An average can hide big differences.

screens.text: Country A: income per person 2,000 USD, life expectancy 75, most adults schooled. Country B: 2,500 USD, life expectancy 55, few schooled. Which likely has the higher HDI?
screens.why: The HDI combines health, education and income. A is far ahead on health and education, which outweighs a small income gap.

notes.text: p.6: "GDP per capital" should be "GDP per capita".

p.8: the HDI is described as a non-monetary index of fertility, mortality and infrastructure. The UNDP HDI combines health (life expectancy), education (years of schooling) and standard of living (GNI per capita, PPP), scaled 0–1. The lesson adds this correction.
The book gives no growth-rate formula; the formula, all worked numbers, the slider and the HDI comparison item are added.
